title: ArchSieve declared dependency rules 0.1
description: Dependency rules declared by the user and checked by `scan --rules <file>`. The vocabulary mirrors dependency-cruiser (forbidden, allowed, from, to, path, pathNot), but paths are regular expressions matched against snapshot node ids (a file path, go:<package>, npm:<package>, nest:...), so one rule language covers every analyzer. Only verifiable edges are checked (imports, nest-imports, nest-injects), and each violation is an error finding.

forbidden.description: An edge that matches a forbidden rule is an error finding whose rule is the rule's name.

name.description: Stable rule id: the finding's rule and the first part of its id. Unique in the file.

allowed.description: When present, an edge that matches no allowed rule is a not-in-allowed error finding (dependency-cruiser semantics).

pattern.description: A regular expression (JavaScript syntax, no flags) matched against a node id, or a list of them (any may match). In to, $1..$9 are replaced by the groups of the from.path match.

end.description: One end of an edge. An empty object matches every node.

pathNot.description: The node id must not match.
